slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 1 — Product Hero & Executive Summary:
- Track & Fit: AgentX Hackathon 2026, Problem Statement PS-04 (Autonomous Support Agent for Online Sellers).
- Team: Team Rookie (3 members).
- Target User: Solo direct-to-consumer (D2C) online merchant managing customer support, shipping, and returns alone.
- Core Insight: Solo sellers lose 15–20 minutes per return navigating fragmented tabs (chat, Shopify, Shippo, return policy), making memory-based decisions without traceable proof.
- Core Thesis: 'Models observe. Code verifies. Seller authorizes.'
- The Console Mockup showcases our core benchmark (Case B): Buyer ordered White Headphones (HEAD-WHT-02, ₹1,499), but unboxing frame 00:07 reveals a Black item. The agent flags the contradiction and presents actionable choices to the seller.
- Safety Boundary: The system never autonomously issues a refund or denies a customer. Financial release strictly requires 1-click merchant authorization.

gap_card.title: NO SHARED EVIDENCE RECORD
gap_card.description: Today the seller opens 4 browser tabs and guesses. An erroneous refund burns inventory margin; an unfair denial destroys repeat customer trust. The gap is the absence of an auditable artifact tying order truth, video keyframes, and policy clauses together before money moves.

slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 2 — Problem Space & The Four Disconnected Sources:
- The returns bottleneck for solo sellers is not an absent returns portal; it is fragmented, unverified context.
- The four disconnected sources:
  1. Buyer claim in chat (unverified claims, emotional text).
  2. Store truth in Shopify (SKU HEAD-WHT-02, ₹1,499).
  3. Courier tracking in Shippo (delivered 4 days ago).
  4. Store return policy document (7-day defect window, security tag).
- Central Gap: Four systems, but no traceable decision. The merchant makes memory-based decisions across multiple tabs.
- Fraud Context (Sourced definitions): NRF 2025 reports 9% for strictly criminal return fraud, whereas Appriss/Deloitte 2024 reports 15.14% when combining fraud and policy abuse (wardrobing, unboxing swaps). These measure distinct scopes and must never be merged.
- Asymmetric Merchant Risk: Wrong refund loses inventory and gross margin; unfair denial destroys customer lifetime value (LTV).

slides.headline: The order says white. The video shows black.
slides.subheadline: ReturnLens flags the contradiction — the seller decides.

decision_panel.title: EVIDENCE ANALYSIS
seller_options: 1. Request unboxing video with packaging label / serial visible
2. Reject return under policy (item does not match order record)
3. Override & approve if seller acknowledges known warehouse mis-shipment
decision_panel.guardrail_note: Automated payout inhibited · Cap: min(₹4,999, remaining, paid) · No autonomous denial

slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 3 — The Star Demo & Technical Honesty in Vision Citation:
- Core Benchmark Scenario (Case B): Buyer ordered White Headphones (HEAD-WHT-02, ₹1,499), but unboxing frame 00:07 shows black headphones.
- Visual Grounding Honesty: The agent does NOT claim to read an unreadable SKU barcode from frame 00:07. It factually observes: 'Observed Color: Midnight Black · Exact SKU: Not verified · Tag: Not visible in cited frame'.
- Decision Logic: Seeing a black item when white was ordered is an undeniable visual contradiction against the manifest. Instead of auto-denying the customer (which might alienate an honest buyer if the warehouse mis-shipped), the policy engine triggers ESCALATE.
- Three Clear Merchant Options:
  1. Request unboxing video with packaging label / serial number visible.
  2. Reject return under policy (item does not match order record).
  3. Override & approve if seller acknowledges known warehouse fulfillment error.
- Financial Guardrail: min(₹4,999, remaining refundable amount, order paid amount). No money moves without seller click.

slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 4 — System Architecture, Agentic Governance & Technical Q&A Defense:
- Philosophy: 'Models observe. Code verifies. Seller authorizes.'
- DEFENSE QUESTION 1: Why is this an agent rather than a hardcoded workflow?
  ReturnLens is an autonomous state machine with dynamic action selection, multi-modal observation, and stateful lifecycle management. In Case C, when a customer submits a dark/blurry video (average brightness 28), the agent does NOT simply fail or run a static linear chain. It inspects the frames, determines evidence is insufficient under Policy P-05, dynamically decides to invoke ask_for_evidence() with specific re-filming guidance, transitions the ticket to WAITING_FOR_EVIDENCE, pauses execution while retaining state and order context, and resumes the exact triage session when new media arrives. Conversely, for routine order status requests, the agent selects the zero-vision fast path directly querying mock APIs.
- DEFENSE QUESTION 2: What happens if vision or critic models hallucinate?
  Vision models produce non-binding observation metadata, never authoritative decisions. Hard business rules (return windows from carrier delivery timestamps, SKU comparisons) are executed in deterministic Python code (P-01 to P-08). The critic provides an adversarial sanity check against cited timestamps. If both vision and critic experience correlated hallucinations, the fail-closed human seller gate guarantees that no refund or return label can ever be issued without seller review.
- DEFENSE QUESTION 3: How do you prevent duplicate or incorrect refunds?
  1. Idempotency keys (hash(order_id, return_id, transaction_type)) prevent double-execution.
  2. Ledgers track cumulative refunded amounts against total order value: 0 < amount <= min(₹4,999, remaining_refundable_amount, order_paid_amount).
  3. LLMs possess zero capability to call payment gateways directly; all actions produce draft state objects awaiting merchant authorization.

slides.headline: Four evidence conditions. Four controlled actions.
slides.subheadline: Expected prototype behaviors across staged benchmark cases. Not measured production metrics.

cases.name: CONSISTENT
cases.subtitle: Clear Defect
cases.observation: Staged casing crack verified in unboxing frame 00:04 · Manifest & return window match.
cases.action_detail: Agent prepares mock shipping label & drafts refund in pending_return_receipt. Money releases only upon warehouse receipt.

cases.name: CONTRADICTION
cases.subtitle: Color Mismatch
cases.observation: White ordered (HEAD-WHT-02) vs Black unboxed in Frame 00:07 · Exact SKU unverified.
cases.action_detail: Policy P-03 blocks automation. Inhibits label and refund. Seller selects 1 of 3 concrete resolution options.

cases.name: UNCLEAR
cases.subtitle: Low Lighting
cases.observation: 4-second dark video, brightness 28/255, barcode obscured · Insufficient visual evidence.
cases.action_detail: Agent calls ask_for_evidence(); transitions ticket to WAITING_FOR_EVIDENCE; resumes context on upload (1 retry limit).

cases.name: SEQUENCE
cases.subtitle: Continuity Check
cases.observation: Staged continuous take from sealed parcel opening to product reveal · Sequence inspected.
cases.action_detail: Expected prototype behavior: inspect sequence continuity and flag missing transitions for seller review.

slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 5 — Four Reproducible Benchmark Scenarios:
- Grounding Note: These four scenarios represent staged prototype test suites and deterministic expected behaviors, NOT ungrounded production field metrics.
- Case 01 (Consistent Claim): All rules pass (within 7d, SKU matches manifest, tag visible, physical crack observed). System drafts return shipping label and refund draft in 'pending_return_receipt' state. No refund money is transferred until physical warehouse receipt.
- Case 02 (Contradiction): Color mismatch detected (ordered white, unboxed black). System prevents auto-rejection and routes to seller review with 3 concrete resolution options.
- Case 03 (Unclear / Agentic Loop): Dark video (28/255 avg brightness). Instead of auto-denying, the agent provides a clear checklist, transitions to WAITING_FOR_EVIDENCE, and resumes on upload (1 retry limit protects customers from infinite loops).
- Case 04 (Continuity): Expected prototype behavior: inspect parcel-to-product sequence to flag suspicious cut-aways or missing transitions.
- Financial Cap Formula: min(₹4,999, remaining refundable amount, order paid amount) strictly prevents over-refunding.

slides.speaker_notes:
Slide 6 — 24-Hour Sprint Feasibility, Ownership & Strict Scope Guardrails:
- Feasibility Argument: Why is ReturnLens realistically buildable in 24 hours by 3 engineers?
  1. No live external production dependencies: deterministic mock APIs for Shopify & Shippo eliminate external latency and flakiness.
  2. Clear division of labor with single-threaded ownership across 3 teammates:
     - Person A (Backend & State Machine): LangGraph orchestrator, mock store/courier APIs, order status fast path, state serialization.
     - Person B (Video Pipeline & UI): FFmpeg keyframe extraction, deterministic rules P-01 to P-08, critic prompt, seller console.
     - Person C (Integration & Validation): Clarification/resume loop, 4 staged demo cases (A-D), authorization boundary tests, demo video recording, README.
  3. Strict Scope Discipline:
     - NEVER CUT: Core policy engine, frame citations, seller authorization gate, structured audit log, clarification/resume loop, 4 demo cases.
     - CUT FIRST IF BEHIND: Real carrier webhooks, multi-product order parsing, video OCR barcode scanning, production payment gateways, seller analytics dashboards.
- Winning Philosophy: 'The winning hackathon agent is not the one with the most tool definitions. It is the one where every action is held to evidence, and the seller stays in control.'
